labels.description: Adds a new disclosure that the current or future listing of Recorded Future as an "undesirable" or "unreliable" entity by certain jurisdictions could further increase information security risk, and escalates AI from threats that "may be further enhanced" by threat actors' use of AI to widespread AI use that "is enhancing" threat frequency and effectiveness and has "further exacerbated" fraud and cyber-attacks.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new exposure tied to a named business (Recorded Future) and adverse jurisdictional listings is disclosed; criterion 3: the AI threat moves from hypothetical to realized; the cross-reference rename to "Privacy, Data, AI and Information Security" and page-header changes are minor on their own.

labels.description: Adds network degradation, updates and migrations to new technology and platforms, and cybersecurity-related disruptions or failures at third-party service providers to the listed causes of service interruptions.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new sources of operational disruption risk are disclosed; the "disaster" to "disasters" change is stylistic.

labels.description: The only change is an inserted page header ("MASTERCARD 2025 FORM 10-K 35 PART I ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS"); the body text, including the five-largest-customers concentration statement, is identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-layout artifact with no change in wording or substance.

labels.description: The reference to bank failures "similar to those that occurred in the U.S. in recent years" drops "in the U.S.", generalizing the precedent for customer consolidation beyond the U.S.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a named jurisdiction (the U.S.) is dropped; criterion 3: the scope of the referenced bank-failure precedent is widened; the page-header removal is minor.

labels.description: The description of domestic switching changes from "with the exception of the U.S. and a select number of other jurisdictions, most in-country transactions" being switched by customers or other processors to Mastercard itself switching "a high percentage of domestic (or in-country) transactions", with customers switching only in "several jurisdictions".
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the scope of the dependency on customers to switch domestic transactions and manage the brand is materially narrowed; criterion 2: the specific U.S. reference is dropped.

labels.description: The only change is an inserted page header ("36 MASTERCARD 2025 FORM 10-K PART I ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS"); the merchant acceptance-cost and incentive text is identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-layout artifact with no change in wording or substance.

labels.description: Adds system integrators and other third party partners as channels through which Mastercard works with governments, both in the introductory scope and in the reputational-risk bullet.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a new category of counterparty is referenced; criterion 3: the scope of government-work exposure is widened; the parenthetical punctuation, page-header removal and paragraph merge are minor.
